newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end volatile day mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end volatile day mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mixed, with Standard & Poor's 500s wrapping up a volatile session slightly firmer.
Traders attributed the late short-covering bounce to short-term technical factors, as December S&Ps became oversold once they dropped to a weekly low of 739.55 in earlier afternoon trade.
In the last 30 minutes of pit trade, December S&Ps climbed to 747.90, below the intraday high of 748.90.

The whipsaw movement in the first half of the session, which initially pulled December to the downside, was linked to arbitrage sell programs as traders tried to adjust the spread between December and cash S&Ps.
December opened below cash S&Ps' Tuesday settlement price of 748.28, instead of trading near its fair value level which is 1.50 points above cash.
The contract's second spike lower occurred as U.S. bond prices continued to decline.
"The break around 1220 CST/1820 GMT was tied to bonds," said Greg Nie, senior vice president at Everen Securities.
T-bonds sharpened losses due to a confluence of factors, including the lack of a coupon pass, higher crude oil prices and the issuance of corporate bonds.
Some analysts were still smarting over IBM's $850 million 100-year debt issuance on Tuesday.

A retest of the intraday low of 739.55 in December S&Ps would be particularly negative in the intermediate term, one floor analyst said. Further support is pegged at 737.00 and the three-week low of 730.40.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were up 2.15 at 747.65, New Composites were 1.15 higher at 394.25, KBT Value Lines rose 1.85 at 683.75, Nikkeis were 60.0 higher at 20,605, Midcap 400s fell 0.75 to 256.55 and Nasdaq 100s were up 0.75 at 835.75.
